newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans fall sharply on Brazil import talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans fall sharply on Brazil import talk.

text.p: CBOT old crop soybean futures fell sharply in fast dealings on Wednesday amid ongoing speculation U.S. crushers would import Brazilian soybeans or soymeal, pit sources said.
That speculation was bolstered by news on Tuesday that poultry producer Tyson Foods, Inc. said it would accept soymeal from U.S. suppliers who crush South American soybeans.
There was talk on the trading floor that up to five cargoes of South American soybeans were heading toward the United States.
In opening trade, Rosenthal Collins sold 1.5 million bushels July while Refco Inc, ADM, and Cargill Inc each sold one million July, pit sources said.
At 0941 CDT, soybeans were down 14 to 4-1/4 cents per bushel with July off 14 at $8.46.
Soymeal was down $4.60 to $0.80 per ton with July down $4.60 at $278.50.
